claims.text: Adding approximately 1–2 vol% finely dispersed copper nanoparticles to the HEA intermediate layer will improve its heat-transfer capability.
Adding approximately 1–2 vol% copper nanoparticles will preserve the structural integrity of the HEA under plasma-facing reactor conditions.
A copper content of approximately 1–2 vol% will create a percolative thermal-conduction network.
The proposed enhancement will persist at approximately 300–600°C.
The proposed enhancement will persist under cyclic thermal-mechanical loading.
Temperatures of 300–600°C and cyclic thermal-mechanical loading are typical operating conditions for intermediate layers in nuclear reactor components.
The copper nanoparticles will segregate to HEA grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary copper nanoparticles will form interconnected paths.
The interconnected copper paths will facilitate electronic and phononic heat transport.
The copper nanoparticle network will not disrupt the bulk mechanical coherence of the HEA matrix.
Copper nanoparticles have inherently high electronic and phononic thermal conductivity.
Homogeneous nanoparticle dispersion will leave the load-bearing framework of the HEA unaltered.
Preserving the HEA load-bearing framework will maintain mechanical strength and resistance to failure under reactor conditions.
The modified HEA will have approximately 30–50% greater thermal conductivity than the baseline intermediate-layer HEA.
The modified HEA's yield strength will remain comparable to or within acceptable limits relative to the original HEA.
The modified HEA's fracture toughness will remain comparable to or within acceptable limits relative to the original HEA.
The baseline HEA without copper has lower heat-transfer capability than the proposed copper-modified HEA.
The claimed performance improvement is intended to remain observable after irradiation-relevant testing.

The hypothesis would be falsified if copper-doped specimens fail to show a statistically significant thermal-conductivity improvement on the order of 30–50% without measurable mechanical-property degradation.
